reuse.why: All weekend/holiday resolution goes through the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and the new range handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule and the same occurrence path as getUpcomingDates.

duplication.why: The 'if skipWeekend then resolve with frequency, mode and holidays, then format the day' wrapper is written three times: inline in getNextDate, resolveSkippedWeekend in schedule-template.ts and getOccurrenceDay in schedules/app.ts.

placement.why: The non-working-day rule, holiday matching and lookahead bounds sit in shared/schedules.ts; the extra per-module wrappers belong there as well.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the schedule date logic, the new handler, the RecurConfig type, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: The core rule is in one function, but each caller still decides the skipWeekend gate and reads frequency/holidays under its own field names, and the lookahead bounds rely on comment-justified heuristics.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every caller still delegates the actual move/skip to getDateWithSkippedWeekend; only the gating wrapper is repeated.

disguised_duplication.where: The same gate-resolve-format logic appears under different names: resolveSkippedWeekend (budget/schedule-template.ts), getOccurrenceDay (schedules/app.ts), and inline in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained frequency and holidays parameters and a daily -> null branch; getNextDate, schedule-template's resolveSkippedWeekend and app.ts's getOccurrenceDay each keep their own skipWeekend gate around it.
